issue.title: sase lsp re-execs itself forever when SASE_XPROMPT_LSP_CMD is 'sase lsp'

task_type_fields.impact: Anyone who sets SASE_XPROMPT_LSP_CMD="sase lsp" (a natural thing to try, since sase-nvim's lsp.lua defaults to `{ "sase", "lsp" }` and its smoke tests honor SASE_XPROMPT_LSP_CMD) gets an editor LSP client that starts but never initializes, with a process spinning in a re-exec loop and no error message. sase doctor's xprompt LSP check also reports the override as the command source without flagging it.
task_type_fields.repro:
Proposed by sase-1co.5 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #1) while smoke-testing sase-nvim LSP alternation tokens; reproduced independently by the sase-1co land agent on 2026-09-29.

```
$ SASE_XPROMPT_LSP_CMD="sase lsp" timeout 8 sase lsp --version </dev/null; echo $?
# prints the sase startup config warning six times (one per re-exec), never prints a version
124
$ SASE_XPROMPT_LSP_CMD="" timeout 8 sase lsp --version </dev/null
sase-xprompt-lsp 0.36.0
```

Root cause: `handle_xprompt_lsp_command` in `src/sase/integrations/xprompt_lsp.py` resolves the server argv via `_resolve_xprompt_lsp_command`, which returns `shlex.split($SASE_XPROMPT_LSP_CMD)` verbatim, then `os.execvp`s it with the environment unchanged (`_prepare_xprompt_lsp_environment` only adds package-dir defaults). When the override names the wrapper itself (`sase lsp`, or any path to the `sase` console script followed by `lsp`), the exec'd process reads the same variable and execs itself again forever: a hot exec loop that re-imports sase each time and never reaches the Rust server.

Suggested fix: before exec, drop `SASE_XPROMPT_LSP_CMD` from the child environment (the Rust server never reads it), or detect an override whose resolved argv is the `sase lsp` wrapper and fall through to the normal binary resolution with a stderr warning. Add a unit test on `_resolve_xprompt_lsp_command` / `_prepare_xprompt_lsp_environment`.

issue.creation_reason: sase-1co.5 proposed this follow-up after an editor LSP client never initialized; the sase-1co land agent reproduced the exec loop, and it is not caused by that epic.

payload.description: Confirm prior lander's follow-up task for sase-1co.5 exists

evidence.note: Relayed from sase-1eq.9 PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP #2 (24 nested spawns with SASE_MACRO_LSP_CMD='sase lsp') and re-reproduced by sase-1eq.land on 2026-10-05 at sase 17c2907d3b after the macro rename: SASE_MACRO_LSP_CMD='sase lsp' timeout 8 sase lsp --version </dev/null exits 124 after printing the startup config warning once per re-exec and never reaches the server, while SASE_MACRO_LSP_CMD='' prints 'sase-macro-lsp 0.36.5'. The wrapper now lives in src/sase/integrations/macro_lsp.py; the fix should drop or guard both SASE_MACRO_LSP_CMD and the flag-gated legacy SASE_XPROMPT_LSP_CMD before exec.
